title: Business licences and clearances in India
summary: The registrations and licences a new business may need: tax, local, labour, industrial, location, environment, factory, excise and import-export.

chunks.heading: Tax and local registrations
chunks.explanation_md:
The slide lists the first licences for a new business in India.

- **PAN Card**: needed because you file your return in your name. The slide says you can apply for Rs.94 and get it in 7 days.
- **TAN**: the Tax Collection and Deduction Account Number.
- **GST Registration**: applies to services, with a threshold of ₹20 lakhs (₹10 lakhs in special states) and rates typically 18%.
- **Shops and Establishment License**: within 30 days of establishing the new enterprise or firm.
- **Professional Tax**: for high-salary professionals as employees. The slide gives the Punjab State Development Tax (PSDT): it applies to employees earning above ₹2,50,000 a year who are taxable under the Income Tax Act, with a monthly deduction of ₹200 per taxable employee.

chunks.heading: Employee and industrial licences
chunks.explanation_md:
The slide continues the list.

- **Trade License**: issued by the municipal authority where trade is conducted, so that the business is carried on according to the relevant rules, standards and safety guidelines.
- **Employee Provident Fund Registration**: with the Employee Provident Fund Organization. It is mandatory if there are more than 20 employees.
- **Employee State Insurance (ESI) Registration**: mandatory if there are 10 employees in a factory or 20 in other establishments.
- **Compulsory industrial license**: under the Industrial (D&R) Act, 1951, for categories such as distillation and brewing of alcoholic drinks, cigars and cigarettes, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, industrial explosives, and hazardous chemicals.

key_terms.meaning: Issued by the municipal authority where trade is conducted, to ensure the business follows the relevant rules, standards and safety guidelines.

chunks.heading: Location, environment and factory rules
chunks.explanation_md:
**Locational restrictions.** The location of industrial units is subject to local zoning, land use and environmental rules. An industrial licence is required if the unit is within 25 km of the standard urban area limits of 23 cities with a population of one million as per the 1991 Census. The restriction does not apply if the unit is in an area designated an "industrial area" before 25th July 1991, or for electronics, computer software and printing and any industry later notified as "non polluting".

**Environmental clearance.** Promoters of projects in specified categories must obtain statutory clearances on pollution control and environment from the Ministry of Environment and Forests under The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. Ecologically fragile locations follow separate guidelines.

**Factory license.** The occupier of a factory needs a licence under the respective State Factories Rules, applied for at the office of the Chief Inspector of Factories.

key_terms.meaning: An industry notified as such is exempt from the locational licence restriction; the slide names electronics, computer software and printing.
Required of the occupier of a factory under State Factories Rules; applied for to the Chief Inspector of Factories.

chunks.heading: Excise and import-export licences
chunks.explanation_md:
**Central Excise License.** Manufacturers of excisable goods, and anyone dealing in them, must register the premises with the Central Excise Department before commencing business, applying to the jurisdictional Central Excise Officer.

**State Excise License.** Alcoholic beverages are a state subject, so rules, duties and taxes vary by state. Anyone dealing in excisable goods registers with State Excise, all brands (local or imported) are registered with each state's Excise Department, and permits are needed to move alcoholic beverages from warehouse to trade.

**Import Export License.** Most goods can be imported freely, but some are prohibited and some need an import licence from the **Director General of Foreign Trade (DGFT)**. Typically the licence is valid for 24 months for capital goods and 18 months for raw materials, components, spare parts and consumables. It has two copies: the **Foreign Exchange Control Copy** (for remittance to the foreign seller or opening a letter of credit) and the **Customs Copy** (shown to Customs to clear the goods). Export licence applications also go to the DGFT, and the Importer Exporter Code comes from the DGFT.

key_terms.meaning: Director General of Foreign Trade, who issues import licences, handles export licence applications and issues the Importer Exporter Code.
The copy of the import licence presented to the Customs authority so they can clear the goods.

chunks.exam_line: Import licence: valid 24 months (capital goods), 18 months (raw materials etc.); two copies, Foreign Exchange Control and Customs.

chunks.heading: Licence lists for a restaurant, a school and a retail store
chunks.explanation_md:
Three slides show how many licences one business type needs, each as a table of licence and issuing authority.

**Restaurant.** Health / Trade License (municipal authority / health department); Eating House License (Police Commissioner); Restaurant Grade License (FDA); Liquor License (Excise Commissioner); Approval / Re-Approval of Restaurants, needed for the liquor licence (Department of Tourism of Government of India in the state); licence to play music (Phonographic Performance Limited / Indian Performing Right Society); Environmental Clearance (Pollution Control Board); NOC from the Fire Department; Signage License (municipal authority); Shop & Establishment License (local municipal corporation).

**School.** Certificate of Registration of Society (Registrar of Societies); Essentiality Certificate, Certificate of Recognition, Certificate of Upgradation and Approved Scheme of Management (Department of Education and municipality as listed); Certificate of Affiliation (an educational board like CBSE or CISCE); site plan, building fitness and building completion certificates (municipality or development authority); Health / Water Testing Report (municipality / water board).

**Retail establishment.** Shop & Establishment License; Labour License / 7 days working permission; Certificate of Recognition (Labour Commissioner); Drug License for OTC products; Weights & Measurement calibration (Local Legal Metrology); Traffic Police NOC (RTO); licence under Essential Commodities; plus municipal permits for frozen non-veg food, freezers and chillers, illuminated showcase, valet parking and storage of inflammable goods.
chunks.exam_line: Different business types need different licence sets: a restaurant needs Eating House and Liquor licences; a school needs Affiliation and Recognition certificates; retail needs Labour and Legal Metrology approvals.

questions.model_answer_md:
Business licences in India cover tax, local rules and employees.

- **Tax**: **PAN Card** (return filed in your name), **TAN**, **GST Registration** (₹20 lakhs threshold, ₹10 lakhs in special states, typically 18%) and **Professional Tax** (for example Punjab State Development Tax, ₹200 a month per taxable employee earning above ₹2,50,000 a year).

- **Employees**: **Employee Provident Fund** registration (mandatory above 20 employees) and **Employee State Insurance** registration (mandatory at 10 employees in a factory or 20 in other establishments).

questions.stem: Explain the import licence: validity, copies and who issues it.
questions.model_answer_md:
India allows free import of most goods, but some categories are prohibited and some are allowed only under an **import licence**.

- **Who issues it**: the Director General of Foreign Trade (DGFT); export licence applications also go to the DGFT, and the Importer Exporter Code comes from it.
- **Validity**: typically 24 months for capital goods and 18 months for raw materials, components, spare parts and consumables.
- **Two copies**: the Foreign Exchange Control Copy, used for remittance to the foreign seller or opening a letter of credit, and the Customs Copy, presented to Customs so they can clear the goods.

questions.stem: A new entrepreneur wants to open a restaurant. Using the deck, discuss the licences and registrations needed and the authority that issues each.
questions.model_answer_md:
Opening a restaurant means collecting a long list of licences. The deck gives a table of **licence and issuing authority**, and general licences that apply to any business.

**Licences for the restaurant itself.**
- **Health / Trade License**: municipal authority or health department.
- **Eating House License**: Police Commissioner.
- **Restaurant Grade License**: FDA.
- **Liquor License**: Excise Commissioner, which needs the **Approval / Re-Approval of Restaurants** from the Department of Tourism of Government of India in the state.
- **License to play music**: Phonographic Performance Limited / Indian Performing Right Society.
- **Environmental Clearance**: Pollution Control Board.
- **NOC from the Fire Department**: State Fire Department.
- **Signage License**: municipal authority.
- **Shop & Establishment License**: local municipal corporation, within 30 days of establishment.

**General registrations.** PAN and TAN for tax; GST registration (₹20 lakhs threshold for services, typically 18%); Trade License; and, depending on staff numbers, Employee Provident Fund (above 20 employees) and Employee State Insurance.

**Alcohol.** Alcoholic beverages are a state subject, so rules and duties vary by state, brands must be registered with the state Excise Department, and permits are needed to move them from warehouse to trade.

In conclusion, the restaurant must clear health, police, food-grade, excise, tourism, music, pollution, fire, signage and shop licences before it can trade.

questions.stem: Discuss the licences and clearances that apply to a manufacturing unit in India: locational, environmental, factory, excise and industrial licences.
questions.model_answer_md:
A manufacturing unit faces several layers of licensing before it can start.

**Industrial licence.** A compulsory industrial licence under the Industrial (D&R) Act, 1951 is required for categories such as distillation and brewing of alcoholic drinks, cigars and cigarettes, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, industrial explosives and hazardous chemicals.

**Locational restrictions.** Location is subject to local zoning, land use and environmental rules. An industrial licence is needed if the unit is within 25 km of the standard urban limits of 23 cities with a population of one million as per the 1991 Census. The restriction does not apply to areas designated "industrial areas" before 25th July 1991, or to electronics, computer software, printing and other industries notified as "non polluting".

**Environmental clearance.** Promoters of projects in specified categories need statutory clearances on pollution control and environment from the Ministry of Environment and Forests under The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. Ecologically fragile locations follow separate guidelines.

**Factory license.** The occupier of a factory obtains a licence under the State Factories Rules from the office of the Chief Inspector of Factories.

**Excise.** Manufacturers of excisable goods must register the premises with the Central Excise Department before commencing business; alcoholic beverages also need State Excise registration.

**Other registrations.** Trade License, PAN, TAN, GST, and Employee State Insurance at 10 employees in a factory.

In conclusion, the unit must clear industrial, location, environment, factory and excise approvals in addition to general tax registrations.
